skill.name: db-handler
skill.description: Plan and edit Drizzle ORM database schemas, including tables, relations, indexes, JSONB validation, and migration workflows.
skill.summary: Guides Drizzle ORM schema design, relations, indexes, and safe database change planning.
skill.author: AayushBaniya2006

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives caused by Markdown code spans for file paths, identifiers, and examples. One finding is confirmed because the skill instructs agents to run npx drizzle-kit push, and a semantic concern is direct schema synchronization without migration review. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation and environment selection before any drizzle-kit push. Prefer reviewed migration files for production changes.
Use a project-local pinned package script instead of ad hoc npx execution when a schema command is needed.
State that destructive schema changes must not run against production unless the user names the target database and approves the operation.

static_findings.snippet: -   **DO** use `npx drizzle-kit push` to sync schema changes directly to the database.
- Use Drizzle's Relational Query API (`with: { ... }`) or explicit `.leftJoin()` to fetch related da
- Avoid breaking changes without explicit confirmation.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks mark a file path in Markdown. There is no instruction to execute this path as a shell command.

The instruction tells the agent to run npx drizzle-kit push, which executes project tooling and can mutate the connected database. This creates integrity and availability risk without explicit safeguards.

semantic_findings.title: Direct Database Schema Push Without Migration Review
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs agents to avoid generated migrations and use npx drizzle-kit push to sync schema changes directly. This can alter database structure without an auditable migration file or production review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow is stated directly in adjacent instructions. It is not evidence of malicious intent, but it is a concrete database integrity risk.

content.value_statement: Database schema changes can create data loss, slow queries, or inconsistent Drizzle definitions. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured schema design, relations, indexes, and review steps.
actual_capabilities: Drafts Drizzle pgTable schemas grouped by domain.
Adds columns, primary keys, timestamps, relations, and foreign keys.
Recommends indexes for joins, filters, and sorting.
Uses Zod typing guidance for JSONB columns.
Explains relational queries and joins to avoid N+1 queries.
Prompts for confirmation before complex or breaking schema changes.
limitations: Does not inspect a live database unless the agent has separate project access.
May suggest direct schema pushes, which need explicit user review.
Does not replace production migration planning or backup procedures.
Does not validate business data rules without domain requirements.

use_cases.title: Create a new domain table
use_cases.description: Plan a Drizzle table with fields, relations, indexes, and review questions before implementation.

use_cases.title: Review schema change safety
use_cases.description: Check a planned column or relation change for migration risk, compatibility, and confirmation needs.

use_cases.title: Improve relational query performance
use_cases.description: Identify missing indexes and N+1 query patterns when related data loads slowly.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Table
prompt_templates.prompt: Use db-handler to draft a Drizzle table for [entity]. Include UUID IDs, timestamps, relations, and indexes. Ask before any database push.

prompt_templates.title: Modify Columns Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Use db-handler to update [table] with [new fields]. Prefer nullable fields or defaults, and identify any breaking change risks.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Related Data Loading
prompt_templates.prompt: Use db-handler to review [query flow]. Find N+1 patterns, missing indexes, and better relation loading options.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Production Migration Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use db-handler to evaluate this schema change for production. List data risks, rollback concerns, confirmation steps, and migration review needs.

output_examples.input: Create a subscriptions table linked to users and plans.
output_examples.output: A proposed table design with key fields, user and plan relations, index recommendations, and a confirmation question before applying changes.

output_examples.input: Our dashboard loads users and their posts slowly.
output_examples.output: A performance review that identifies likely N+1 access, recommends relation loading or joins, and lists indexes for common filters.

output_examples.input: Add settings to each organization record.
output_examples.output: A safe column plan that recommends JSONB validation, nullable rollout options, and checks for production migration risk.

best_practices: Confirm the target environment before syncing or migrating schema changes.
Index foreign keys, frequent filters, and common sort fields when designing tables.
Define JSONB validation with Zod before storing structured settings.
anti_patterns: Running schema push commands before the user confirms the table design.
Adding JSONB fields for unrelated data that should be normalized.
Fetching related records inside loops instead of loading them in one query.

faq.question: Can this skill change my database automatically?
faq.answer: It can suggest schema commands, but changes should require explicit user confirmation and project access.

faq.question: Does it support Drizzle ORM?
faq.answer: Yes. The instructions focus on Drizzle ORM tables, relations, indexes, and relational query patterns.

faq.question: Can Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. It is described for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it create migration files?
faq.answer: The skill discourages generated migrations, so production users should add their own migration review process.

faq.question: Does it handle JSONB columns?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires Zod schema guidance for JSONB columns before storing structured data.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when planning tables, relations, indexes, schema updates, or Drizzle query performance improvements.
